items.stem: On the interval $0\le x<2\pi$, where are all of the vertical asymptotes of $y=\tan x$?
items.hint: Rewrite tangent as a quotient of sine and cosine, then ask which of the two being zero is what breaks the fraction.
worked: Write $\tan x=\dfrac{\sin x}{\cos x}$, so the graph breaks exactly where $\cos x=0$.
On the unit circle, $\cos x$ is the $x$-coordinate, and it is $0$ at $x=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ and at $x=\dfrac{3\pi}{2}$.
Neither value is cancelled by anything, so both are vertical asymptotes: $x=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ and $x=\dfrac{3\pi}{2}$.

options.text: There are none; $y=\tan x$ is defined for every real number.

items.stem: A student finds the vertical asymptotes of $y=\csc(2x)$ in three lines, where $n$ stands for any integer. Line 1: $\csc(2x)=\dfrac{1}{\sin(2x)}$. Line 2: an asymptote occurs where $\sin(2x)=0$, so $2x=\pi n$. Line 3: therefore $x=2\pi n$. Which choice names the first line that is wrong and corrects it?
items.hint: Test her final formula against the graph: does every value it produces give a zero denominator, and does it catch all of them?
worked: Line 1 is the correct reciprocal identity, and $\sin u=0$ exactly when $u=\pi n$, so Line 2 is right as well.
Line 3 undoes the $2$ backwards. From $2x=\pi n$, divide both sides by $2$ to get $x=\dfrac{\pi n}{2}$.
Check it: $x=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ makes $\sin(2x)=\sin(\pi)=0$, so it is an asymptote, yet $x=2\pi n$ never produces it.
The first error is in Line 3, and the asymptotes are $x=\dfrac{\pi n}{2}$.

options.text: Line 3; dividing $2x=\pi n$ by $2$ gives $x=\dfrac{\pi n}{2}$.
Line 2; a zero denominator does not force an asymptote, so $y=\csc(2x)$ has no vertical asymptotes.
No line is wrong; the asymptotes really are $x=2\pi n$.

items.stem: Which statement about the graph of $y=\cot\left(2x-\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)$ is true?
items.hint: Factor the coefficient of $x$ out of the inside expression before you read the shift off, and remember that cotangent repeats every $\pi$, not every $2\pi$.
worked: Cotangent repeats every $\pi$, so with $b=2$ the period is $\dfrac{\pi}{b}=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$.
The factored inside reads $x-\dfrac{\pi}{6}$, and the input that makes it zero is $x=\dfrac{\pi}{6}$, so the graph slides $\dfrac{\pi}{6}$ to the right.

options.text: Its period is $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$, and it is the graph of $y=\cot(2x)$ shifted $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ to the right.
Its period is $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$, and it is the graph of $y=\cot(2x)$ shifted $\dfrac{\pi}{6}$ to the right.
Its period is $2\pi$, and it is the graph of $y=\cot(2x)$ shifted $\dfrac{\pi}{6}$ to the right.
Its period is $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$, and it is the graph of $y=\cot(2x)$ shifted $\dfrac{\pi}{6}$ to the left.
